subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I should keep this economical but solid: a self-contained SDK module with a chassis root, spinning wheel joints, a lofted body, cab, weapon-equipped bed, neon strips, and SVG decal textures like emblems, hazard stripes, and license plates, finished with metallic paint customization.

Working out the specific dimensions, wheel count and joint orientations, plus a custom paint function blending gunmetal panels, grime, and highlights, alongside hazard stripe decals.

For the neon accents I'm picking flat glow-friendly colors—cyan, magenta, amber—then blocking out the hull and cab geometry, building the lower hull as a wedge-nosed box and extruding a side profile for the angled crew cab silhouette.

Still assembling vehicle pieces...

Turret with yaw/pitch joints and twin glowing barrels, rear thrusters, magenta tail lights, plus decal planes for the hexagon "77" emblem, hazard stripes, license plate, and flank text, all placed along the body's x-axis bounds with wheels positioned just outside.

Now I'm positioning the wheels along three axles (roughly z=2.1, -0.1, -2.3) with hub radius 0.6, and working out the hull's vertical placement with the belly at 0.75 and top at 1.35, centering the frame around y=0.7 for the chassis joint.

Next I'm shaping the cab and bed: defining a wedge-shaped cab from z -0.3 to 1.5 with a sloped windshield rising to the roof, a hood extending forward, and a bed section toward the rear with walls up to y=1.9. I'm sketching the cab's cross-section profile as a polygon tracing the floor, hood, windshield slope, roof, and back panel.

For the windshield, I'm working out how to position and tilt a thin glass box so its angled surface matches the slope between the hood and roof, calculating the rotation around the X-axis needed to align the box's face normal with the diagonal direction between those two points.

For the side windows, I'm placing thin tinted glass boxes along the cab's sides, checking their vertical span against the roofline and windshield slope to make sure they fit under the roof without clipping.

Now shifting to the wheels: I'm setting up a tire geometry as a flattened cylinder with hub offsets scaled by the vehicle's half-width, adding a rim cylinder, a neon torus ring positioned just outside the rim for glow accents, plus bolts, spokes, and tread blocks arranged radially around the tire. I'm also adding fender boxes positioned above each wheel to cover them.

I'm placing fender boxes to arch over the tire tops with overlapping lip pieces that connect back to the hull, then adding sloped skirt armor panels between the wheels and underglow strip boxes along the lower sides. Now I'm starting a hull paint function that defines seam patterns using surface coordinates and noise.

I'm checking the barrel placement so it clears the cab roof instead of colliding with it, adjusting its z-position and length to sit above the roof height while still reading as a reasonably sized turret barrel.

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy with explicit bone and pitch/yaw rotation axes, then placing rear thrusters as bell-shaped lathes with glowing discs, and adding roof details like a light bar, dome, antenna, and small missile pods mounted on either side.

For decals, I'm designing a hexagonal emblem with "77" text, hazard stripes, and license plate text, placing door decals as forward-facing planes on the cab sides and a hazard strip on the front bumper.

Now I'm laying out the truck bed: side decals with mirrored "NOMAD" text on the bed walls, plus the floor, side walls, rear wall, vertical ribs, and cargo like crates and a fuel can sitting in the open bed.

I'm now shaping the front nose as a tapered frustum box running along the z-axis, with the lower hull extending as one long box across the vehicle's length.

For the front details, I'm adding grille slits with glowing cyan bars, amber headlight slits, a spiked ram bumper, and a hazard decal, then placing a dome sensor and roof lightbar on top.

I'm also adding side mirror cameras, vertical exhaust stacks behind the cab with glowing tips, antenna whips, and hexagonal ERA armor plates on the hood, aiming for roughly 200 parts total, with helper functions for boxes and cylinders to keep the code organized using flat colors.

I'm checking ground clearance math so tire treads and hub radius sink just slightly into the ground for realism without looking wrong, then setting up wheel joints with simple axis directions and planning rotations for the exhaust cylinders.

Writing tread block positions...
